  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "explanation":"stolen_card",
      "likelihood":"high",
      "reasoning":"The issuing-country/IP mismatch and failed address verification support card misuse, reinforced by failed issuer/identity verification. The failure decides the disposition but does not establish the precise fraud mechanism."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"traveller",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"A legitimate customer travelling abroad could explain the foreign IP and address-verification failure. However, the completed identity check failed, so this explanation cannot support clearance under the policy."
    }

  "disposition":"decline",
  "citations":["R03","FP-2 §6.2","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.4","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(b)","FP-2 §6.5(b)","FP-2 §4.2"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R03 holds: the card issuing country differs from the IP country and AVS failed. Card is the only adverse family; all other rule conditions are unmet. No household exception or earlier settling outcome applies. Row §6.6(b) applies, with the failed required id_check deciding the order under §5.3(b). Recommend decline; escalation is prohibited without Linkage, and further verification cannot change the prescribed disposition. Legitimate travel is a plausible competing explanation for the geography, but it does not override failed verification. The order remains unshipped, so decline can prevent fulfilment. This recommendation is advisory."
